query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of Hf to the NbMoTaW alloy can improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy NbMoTaW
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Hf
generation.structural_mediator: Precipitation of intermetallic compounds such as Hf-rich phases
generation.mechanism: Solution strengthening and interface strengthening due to the precipitation of Hf-rich phases
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature ductility without compromising high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance
generation.boundary: The amount of Hf added should be small enough not to significantly reduce the ductility of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Hf required to achieve the desired improvement in room-temperature ductility is uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile tests at room temperature and 1600 °C, and irradiation resistance tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Hf does not improve the room-temperature ductility of the NbMoTaW alloy, or if it compromises its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The NbTaHfTiZr HEA has received a lot of interests among all RHEAs, since it has a totally disordered BCC solid-solution structure with a melting point of about 1800 °C [,]. At normal temperature and cryogenic temperatures, the NbTaHfTiZr RHEA combines excellent strength and ductility []. The NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 RHEA based on this alloy not only maintains excellent room-temperature plasticity but also further improves its strength and has a good cold workability []. In order to explore the potential of the NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 RHEA for high-temperature applications, it is very necessary to study its mechanical properties at high temperatures. Here, we explore the mechanical properties of the NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy from RT to 1227 K and analyze its microscopic deformation mechanism. At the same time, we construct the constitutive equation of this alloy through a stress–strain curve in a deformation temperature range of 873–1173 K and a 0.001–0.1 s−1 strain-rate range and quantify the relationship between the strength and temperature.

As we all know, the alloying of metals with certain specific elements can very effectively improve alloy properties through various strengthening methods such as precipitation strengthening, solution strengthening, and interface strengthening [,,,]. Hf is an essential alloying element for both the interface strengthening of superalloys and the strengthening of the Ni-Al B2 phase [,,,,,]. Recently, some studies have shown that adding a small amount of Hf to a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy could improve the room-temperature mechanical property of the alloy without significantly reducing the ductility of the alloy through the precipitation of intermetallic compounds such as Ni7Hf2 and Laves phases [,]. However, these studies mainly focus on single-phase high-entropy alloys, and the addition of Hf is relatively large, usually more than one atom. Therefore, the effect of trace Hf addition on the properties of the alloy at room temperature and high temperature is worthy of in-depth investigation.
